articles.headline: Alien: Isolation 2 Fans Cheer as Devs Confirm ‘Core Pillar'
keyFacts: Creative Assembly confirmed that Alien: Isolation 2 will receive a physical release, stating that staying true to the analogue nature of the franchise is a core pillar.
The sequel is scheduled for release in 2027 and follows a new protagonist named Blake, who explores a remote world with a Weyland-Yutani survey team.
Gameplay previews feature a dynamic weather system that a smart Xenomorph can exploit to hunt players.
body: As major corporations like Sony and Microsoft continue to push the games industry towards an all-digital future, players are left wondering whether the next title they are excited about will even get a physical release. Thankfully, Creative Assembly has some good news for everyone who has been eagerly awaiting Alien: Isolation 2.

Alien: Isolation, Creative Assembly's 2014 foray into the horror franchise created by Ridley Scott, was a cult hit that used incredible attention to detail to capture the same sense of wonder as the first Alien film. Alien: Isolation 2 was teased in 2024, a decade after the original game's release. As we get closer to launch, Creative Assembly has confirmed that the sequel will get a physical release.

The good news was announced in a short and sweet video on the game's official X account. Creative Assembly said, "staying true to the analogue nature of Alien is one of our core pillars." Notably, the post did not clarify anything beyond saying "physical release," so let's hope that means it will actually include the game on disc or cartridge rather than being merely a box with a download code. Alien: Isolation 2 is due out sometime in 2027, though Creative Assembly has not announced an official release date.
What will Alien: Isolation 2 be about?

Alien: Isolation 2 seems to take place just a few months after the conclusion of the first game. The new protagonist is Blake, a member of a Weyland-Yutani survey team exploring a remote world. Blake and her crew discover the wreckage of a crashed ship, which Amanda Ripley and the Xenomorph were seen aboard at the end of the first game. While Creative Assembly insists Blake is the new protagonist, people aren't convinced we've seen the last of Amanda, who narrated a demo of the game shown to the press.

Gameplay previews have focused on showing off a hostile with a dynamic weather system that a smart Xenomorph can exploit to hunt you down. Creative Assembly says the original movie is still the main inspiration, but both the story and world of Alien: Isolation 2 give me major Alien: Covenant vibes, which is a good thing. Fans have been waiting over a decade for the next chapter in the Alien: Isolation story, and it sure looks like it will be worth the wait.

articles.headline: Marvel Actor Simu Liu Confirms He Wasn’t In Talks For Mass Effect: Universe Despite Striking Resemblance To Character In Leaked Trailer
keyFacts: A trailer for the cancelled game Mass Effect: Universe leaked online following BioWare's closure on October 21.
Fans noticed the game's protagonist strongly resembled actor Simu Liu, who had posted about the studio closure hours earlier.
Simu Liu confirmed to Kotaku that he was not involved with the game and was not in talks with BioWare.
body: Following the studioâs closure on October 21, a trailer for BioWareâs now-cancelled Mass Effect: Universe mysteriously appeared online. In many ways, the trailer was the final twist of the knife, as it looked like BioWare was cooking up something special with the fifth Mass Effect.

Ultimately, however, the most frustrating thing was that, like all good trailers, it left us with more questions than answers. Questions such as âHow would this have tied into the ending of Mass Effect 3?â, âWho fixed the mass relays?â, and âHoly shit, was that Simu Liu?!â

After the trailer leaked online, many immediately pointed out that Mass Effect: Universeâs new protagonist bore a striking resemblance to Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten RingsÂ star Simu Liu. The voice obviously wasnât his, but those chiseled-looking cheekbones were a 1-to-1 match.

The fact that Simu Liu also expressed his adoration of BioWare and his displeasure at the studioâs closure in a post on Threads, hours before the trailer leaked, further fueled fansâ suspicion. Likewise, Liu also seemed a little confused about the characterâs appearance in a reply to the leaked trailer on X.
â¦ waaaaait a minuteâ¦.
— Simu Liu (@SimuLiu) October 24, 2026

Kotaku reached out to Liu in an attempt to figure out if BioWare had contacted him about potentially starring in the game, or even just using his likeness for the protagonistâs default character model.

Funnily enough, in the statement provided to Kotaku, Liu seemed just as confused about his Mass Effect: Universe facsimile as the rest of us: âHaha no, I wasnât involved but youâre not the only one to ask!”

Considering we know that the leaked trailer was only supposed to be shared internally as a proof-of-concept for Electronic Arts executives, I think there are two explanations we can glean from Liuâs confirmation: either the resemblance was a complete coincidence, or BioWare was planning to contact Liu about the potential partnership at a later date.

But hey, considering fans have already thrown enough money at the âSave Mass Effectâ crowdfunder to purchase a billboard, maybe thereâs still a chance that we might see Liu in something Mass Effect-shaped in the future.

articles.headline: College football Week 9 picks, odds: Best bets for Saturday's games
keyFacts: Yahoo Sports published two college football best bets for Week 9 involving Temple playing East Carolina and Oregon State playing Fresno State.
For the first game, the publisher recommended betting over 49.5 points because Temple struggles defensively and East Carolina plays at a fast tempo.
For the second game, the publisher recommended betting under 57.5 points due to Fresno State's strong defense, slow tempo, and likely rain.
body: Some weeks we get marquee matchups sneaking in value on games you were already going to watch, and some weeks we head over to East Carolina for value.
This week, that means a wager involving a Temple team that just gave up 38 to Charlotte, and going under against an Oregon State team whose last three games had point totals of 82, 80 and 78.
Here are two of my favorite Week 9 college football wagers.
Temple at East Carolina (-6.5, 49.5)
Charlotte came to Philadelphia two weeks ago at 0-6, having been outscored 109-18 in its previous two games, and put up 38 points on Temple (2-5).

Owls head coach K.C. Keeler didn't dress it up. "That was the single most embarrassing game I've ever coached," he said, and by Tuesday the defensive line coach was gone, the defensive coordinator had been moved to coaching safeties and Henry Baker was calling the defense. That's the side of this I'm betting on.

Temple's defense ranks No. 130 (of 138) on our board, it has given up 72 points in its last two games and Keeler's own scouting report this week was blunt: "We don't tackle very well. The lack of communication is staggering." A bye week and a new play-caller might fix some of that, but it's rarely fixed in one game. The other side is why this isn't a 56 already.
East Carolina (3-4) ranks No. 117 in offense on our board, and the Pirates have changed quarterbacks twice this season, but they just put 34 on Memphis.

The Pirates plays at the ninth-fastest tempo in the country on our board, so there are plenty of snaps to go around, and RB TJ Engleman Jr. is averaging 6.0 yards a carry. Temple is a runnning team as well, averaging 202 rushing yards a game, and QB Ajani Sheppard has eight touchdown passes without an interception. The Owls put up 455 yards against Charlotte and 437 at UConn, and their last two games had 69 and 54 total points.
We make it East Carolina 31, Temple 25, opening value on the over in this matchup.
Oregon State (-5.5, 57.5) at Fresno State

This number makes sense if you only watched the highlights. Oregon State (5-2) has won five straight, QB Braden Atkinson leads the country with 2,604 passing yards and has gone over 300 in seven straight games, and Jesse Legree was the first receiver in the country to 1,000 yards. The last three Beavers games finished at 82, 80 and 78 points. DraftKings opened this total at 56.5 and it's up to 57.5.

Now check the opponents: Those three games were against Colorado State, San Diego State and Washington State, whose defenses rank 137th, 115th and 99th on our board, and the other two wins came against FCS Montana and a UTEP defense ranked 135th. Against the two real defenses on the schedule — Houston at No. 19 and Texas Tech at No. 27 — the Beavers scored 20 and 24 points.
Fresno State's defense we rank 51st — it's the best one Oregon State has seen since Texas Tech came to Corvallis in September.

Fresno State (4-3) is the other half of this under play, and it's coming off a bye after two straight losses. The Bulldogs rank No. 89 in offense and No. 124 in tempo on our board, which means fewer possessions and shorter games. Their last one was a 26-23 loss at San Diego State in which QB Jayden Mandal threw for 141 yards and was sacked six times, and after the Aztecs kicked a 53-yard field goal with 57 seconds left, the Fresno State offense managed 3 yards on four plays and turned it over on downs.
Matt Entz knows what's coming. "Explosive, pass-first kind of mentality," he said describing the Beavers this week. "We need to do a really good job of trying to keep them behind the chains."

His defense had six sacks and two forced fumbles against San Diego State, so that's not an empty plan. Then there's the weather. The National Weather Service has rain likely in Fresno Saturday night: a 70% chance with a low around 53, for an 8 p.m. local kick on USA Network. That's a pass-first offense throwing in the rain against the best defense it has faced since September, with a slow-tempo offense on the other sideline.
We make it Oregon State 29, Fresno State 24 in what could be the most contrarian spot on the Week 9 slate, fading Oregon State's offense.

articles.headline: Brewers World Series parade 2026 date, time, route and how to watch Milwaukee championship celebration
keyFacts: The Milwaukee Brewers won their first World Series championship in franchise history with a postseason record of 11-2.
The championship parade is scheduled for Friday, October 30, starting at 10 a.m. CT at 4th Street and Wisconsin Avenue.
The parade route concludes at Maier Festival Park for a championship rally, and the event will be broadcast on multiple MLB platforms.
body: The Milwaukee Brewers have done it, completing their first World Series championship in franchise history. Now, it's time to celebrate.

The Brewers will head back to Milwaukee to give fans a championship parade, something that those fans have done recently. This will be the first Milwaukee parade since 2021, when the Bucks won the NBA title, and the third since 2011, when the Green Bay Packers won their last Super Bowl.

This World Series run is historic, as the Brewers ended the postseason with an 11-2 record. Combine that with the team's 103 wins in the regular season, and this is certainly a season worth celebrating.
Here's a look at when and where the Brewers will be celebrating their title.
When is the Brewers World Series parade?
- Date: Friday, Oct. 30
- Time: 10:00 a.m. CT

The Brewers will celebrate their championship with a parade in the city of Milwaukee on Friday, October 30, just a few days after clinching the World Series title. The parade will begin at 10:00 a.m. local time and last into the afternoon.
Brewers World Series parade route

The Brewers' parade will begin on 4th St. and Wisconsin Avenue, where the team will start its journey through the city. The parade will head east before turning north on Jefferson St., then east on Mason St., south on Jackson St., and east on Chicago St.
Finally, the parade will conclude at Maier Festival Park, which is holding a rally that begins at 8:00 a.m. CT. That is presumably where the team will give its speeches to wrap up the day.

articles.headline: I'm calling it: GTA 6 is officially an immersive sim, based on what you can do with NPCs
keyFacts: Rockstar head of development Phil Hooker described clearing witnesses from a store in Grand Theft Auto 6 by provoking NPCs and then defusing the situation so they would leave.
Hooker stated that testing focuses on trying different ways to interact with NPCs and combine game features in unexpected ways.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is rumored to arrive on PC relatively quickly following its console launch.
body: I don't mean to be contrarian (which is rare for me), but I've been generally unfazed by the hype for Grand Theft Auto 6. It's not that I don't think it'll be good—I'm actually damn near certain it will—it's just that none of what Rockstar has focused on so far in its marketing speaks to me all that much.

Anyway, throw those equanimous sentiments out the window, because an anecdote from Edge magazine's new mondo-feature on GTA 6 has convinced me this game is actually an immersive sim, and now I'm bouncing off the walls in anticipation. Chatting about his experience actually playing the game, Rockstar head of development Phil Hooker told a story about the time he deployed a bit of unorthodox crowd control to prepare a store for a heist.

"Recently I was robbing a store that was full of people," said Hooker. "I wanted to get rid of them, because they'd be witnesses who would cause me trouble." What did he do? Well, in GTAs of yore, your options would have been pretty limited, but GTA 6's dovetailing systems gave our man an opportunity. "I basically started picking fights with them, provoking them and then immediately defusing it.

"I didn't actually get them into a fight—I'd just go: 'Ah, sorry, leave it'. Then they would leave the store, so that would clear them out and I could rob it more cleanly." It's one of the things Hooker says he, and Rockstar generally, focuses on in testing: "meeting new NPCs, for example, trying different ways in which to interact with them, trying to find ways to combine the features in ways we maybe haven't thought about."

Forgive me, but is that not the most immersive sim stuff you've ever heard? A sandbox crammed with systems that can collide—or be manipulated—in ways the developers themselves never even expected, to the delight and satisfaction of a creative player? I say it is, and it's quite honestly made me more excited for Rockstar's quadrillion-dollar baby than any glossy trailer. Put it in my hands, please, and then let me use those hands to pick up a crate that turns translucent when I do it.
Rumor has it that GTA 6 will come to PC relatively quickly after the console launch, though Rockstar typically puts at least seven months between console and PC launches.

His most profound loves are for CRPGs, immersive sims, and any game whose ambition outstrips its budget. He thinks you're all far too mean about Deus Ex: Invisible War.

articles.headline: From early to late game, here are the best locations to farm EXP and MRP in Final Fantasy Resonance
keyFacts: Players in Final Fantasy Resonance can farm large amounts of EXP by defeating Metal Minituars, Metal Cactuars, and Metal Gigantuars at specific locations.
Metal enemies yield high EXP rewards but take only one damage per hit and escape quickly, requiring multi-hit abilities to defeat them.
Regular Cactuars and Gigantuars serve as the best targets for farming MRP to master Visions fast in the game.
body: Thanks to its Vision system and steep difficulty curve, finding the right places to farm EXP and MRP can be considered a must if you want to stay ahead and truly bring your builds to life in Final Fantasy Resonance .

And the great thing is, like with the Metal Slimes in Dragon Quest XI , being able to level up fast is only a matter of finding the right spawn spots. No matter if you are in the early or late game, here are the best locations to farm EXP and MRP in Final Fantasy Resonance .

All Metal Cactuar locations
All Metal Gigantuar locations
The best locations to farm MRP in Final Fantasy Resonance Where to find Cactuars and Gigantuars early in FF Resonance
The best locations to farm EXP in Final Fantasy Resonance

Screenshot by Destructoid When looking to farm EXP in FF Resonance , Metal Minituars, Metal Cactuars, and Metal Gigantuars are the main targets and reward you with 2.500, 25.000, and 150.000 EXP per battle (bonuses aside).

You can defeat the metal enemies fast by spamming multi-hit abilities and using both Double Action and Double Cast. Remember, each hit against them will only do 1 DMG, and they will usually escape after a few turns. It is also possible to get double EXP from the battles by using the Mastery Pendant.
All Metal Minituar locations

Available as soon as you unlock the full map, you can find Metal Minituars in a small valley south of the Darven Forge at Dirnado, the Continent of Wind. They will be fairly easy to beat and only demand nine hits.
Screenshot by Destructoid All Metal Cactuar locations

Only available past the mid-game point at the start of Chapter 5, Metal Cactuars can be found on an island west of Mysidia. While there, make sure to also interact with the blizzard whirlwind to take on Shiva’s trial and unlock her as a summon.
All Metal Gigantuar locations

Only spawnable after reaching Chapter 6, you can find and farm Metal Gigantuars by heading to the small island below, located on the west end of Kingdom of Pharm. Apart from the Metal Gigantuar, the area is also known for spawning Gigantuars, as well as the King Gil Snapper needed for the Struck Gold trophy/achievement.

Screenshot by Destructoid Just keep in mind that you cannot land on the island with the airship and must cross the level 52 Dragon’s Maw dungeon to reach it. The dungeon is infested with high-level enemies and welcomes you with an unskippable level 52 Intangir boss fight.

The best locations to farm MRP in Final Fantasy Resonance

Screenshot by Destructoid If you are looking to master your Visions fast in FF Resonance , regular Cactuars and Gigantuars are your best bet and reward you with 429 and 1170 MPR (Expert) per win, respectively.

Unlike their metal variants, the plantoids can be defeated by quickly staggering them with Water attacks, so don’t forget to equip the Azure Amulet on any Double Action character for an easier time. The Gigantuars are also weak to Blizzard and offer Magicite as a rare stealable.
Where to find Cactuars and Gigantuars early in FF Resonance

Thanks to both its ease of access and spawn rate, the spot below, located south of the Sanctum of Y’Shtola in Zoldaad Empire Territory, is the best area to farm Cactuars before acquiring the airship in Chapter 5.

Screenshot by Destructoid Once you can take to the skies, however, the island below, located on Dirnado, the Continent of Wind, becomes the go-to spot for farming MRP. The location spawns both regular Cactuars and Gigantuars (after Chapter 6) and is considered ideal for those not looking to go through Dragon’s Maw.

articles.headline: Brewers manager Pat Murphy takes shot at ‘horseshit’ Yankees team after World Series win
keyFacts: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy criticized the New York Yankees in a video after his team clinched the World Series.
Murphy told impending free agent Jake Bauers to remember playing for the Yankees when they were playing for themselves.
Bauers previously played for the Yankees in 2023 before joining the Brewers and achieving career bests.
body: Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy was captured taking a shot at a “horseshit Yankees team” after he celebrated his team clinching the World Series on Wednesday night.

A video of Murphy talking to Jake Bauers emerged in which the manager tells the Brewers’ soon to be a free agent: “You’re going to be a rich fucker. Just remember when you were on that horseshit Yankees team and you guys were all playing for yourself? Just remember, say, ‘This is the way we used to do it.’”

Bauers played for the Yankees in 2023 before he was traded to the Brewers. The Yankees finished fourth in the AL East in 2023, missing the playoffs for the first time since 2016. Bauers did little to help them, batting .202 with 12 home runs in 84 games that season. However, he has thrived at the Brewers: in the 2026 regular season he hit .266 with 26 home runs and an OPS of .874, all career bests. He was also named the National League Championship Series MVP as the Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers to reach the World Series for the first time since 1982.
Murphy also had another excellent season and is favorite to be named the NL Manager of the Year for a third season in a row.

Murphy is not the first person to joke about the Yankees in a World Series. When the Dodgers overwhelmed the Yankees in the 2024 edition, Los Angeles veteran Joe Kelly said New York were “sloppy” and “can’t make a play”, while his teammate Miguel Rojas called out their “lazy” defense.

articles.headline: EA's sale to Saudi-led consortium was "final nail in the coffin" for BioWare, says studio co-founder
keyFacts: BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk said the studio's closure is sad and called EA's sale to a Saudi-involved consortium the final nail in the coffin.
Zeschuk stated that BioWare's closure impacts the city of Edmonton, which once saw the studio as a beacon of hope.
Zeschuk and fellow co-founder Ray Muzyka retired from BioWare in 2012, and Zeschuk has since focused on his beer-brewing company.
body: One of BioWare's famous doctor-founders, Greg Zeschuk, has finally spoken about the studio's closure last week, saying it's "kind of sad" and that EA's leveraged buyout by a Saudi-involved consortium "was the final nail in the coffin".

Speaking to 80 Level, Zeschuk - who founded BioWare in 1995 with fellow medical students Ray Muzyka and Augustine Yip - said he was fishing when news of the studio's closure broke. "I got like 10 texts," Zeschuk said. "I came off the river and got to my little room and opened my phone, and it's like, 'I'm so sorry to hear about BioWare.' And I'm like, 'Oh shit.'"

By the time he flew home later, he'd already apparently digested the news and missed most of the discourse around it. "I wasn't there to share in the moment," he said, "which in some ways was nice because I was able to kind of just take my time with it.
"I've kind of gone through all the emotions long, long ago" -Greg Zeschuk

"I'm not saying it doesn't hurt and doesn't suck," he added. "And I think it's kind of sad. It's actually, in some ways, saddest for the city of Edmonton, where we're from, because we were kind of this beacon of hope and excitement and possibility. We showed you could do something really special in a place that was not known for doing things like that."

Zeschuk and Muzyka retired from BioWare in 2012, the year Mass Effect 3 was released, so they've been away from the business for a considerable amount of time. They've moved on. "I've kind of gone through all the emotions long, long ago," Zeschuk explained.

BioWare did change thereafter, he seemed to accept, but as a result of a gradual change propelled naturally by people leaving and other people coming in. "I'm not going to have so much hubris to say Ray and I were the lynchpin in the chain, our departure ruined everything," he said. "It wasn't that at all. It's a slow and insidious kind of thing and again, it's the people. The people are the key."

When he heard the private acquisition of EA had gone through, that's when he feared things might be headed to a bad place. "I think it was the final nail in the coffin," he said. "I think that was the crux of it in a sense. BioWare makes these kinds of unusual games that take a long time and they're complicated and so it's easier just to pump out sports games every year, and that's a better business model in some ways."

Elsewhere in the interview, Zeschuk talked a little about the origins of BioWare selling to EA in 2008 - "We had options actually" - and about personally sliding away from story-driven games towards more action-centred games like the Nioh series and Elden Ring.

Since 2017, Zeschuk has been building a beer-brewing company called Blind Enthusiasm, which apparently now employs a dozen people and ships tens of thousands of bottles of beer a year. This interview is the only one Zeschuk has given. Muzyka has so far declined to be interviewed. The third BioWare co-founder, Augustine Yip, left the company long ago, back in 1998.

body: The investigation into whether Rep. Ilhan Omar , D-Minn., married her brother in an alleged immigration fraud scheme in 2009 began under former President Barack Obama in 2016, Fox News Digital has confirmed.
A U.S. Attorney in Minnesota, appointed by then-President Joe Biden, eventually shut down the probe in 2021, a source familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital.

Now, the issue has been thrust back into the spotlight as part of a new federal investigation into the Somali-born congresswoman, part of which centers on whether she or her father committed immigration fraud on her application to become a U.S. citizen.
REP ILHAN OMAR'S IMMIGRATION HISTORY FACES NEW SCRUTINY AS FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS SUBPOENA RELATIVES
Sources previously told Fox News Digital that Omar's "real name" is Ilhan Nur Said Elmi. In a federal court document, she was called "Ilhan Omar Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Omar."
In 2009, Omar, then a U.S. citizen, legally married a man with that surname, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi. The pair officially split in 2017.

The New York Times first reported that Obama's FBI and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) began the probe in the summer of 2016, and that officials "found some evidence that [the marriage] was fraudulent." The Times reported that the investigation concluded when officials decided the potential felony crime was past the statute of limitations.
OMAR’S DELETED TWEET COULD GIVE CLUE ON ALLEGED MARRIAGE TO HER BROTHER

Despite his own administration's investigation into Omar at the time she was running for the Minnesota House, Obama condemned the renewed probe, which included a Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) raid on her Washington, D.C. home on Oct. 12. Federal authorities confiscated her passport, personal phone and computer in the raid.

"It is a basic principle of American democracy that the government can’t selectively target individuals simply because of their political beliefs or what they say," Obama wrote in an X post after the raid earlier this month. "But that’s exactly what the Trump Administration is doing to Congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota."
OBAMA'S LENGTHY REACTION TO OMAR INVESTIGATION TRIGGERS INSTANT BACKLASH: 'SPARE ME'
Obama claimed the Trump administration was targeting Omar because she is a vocal critic of the current president.
"Think about that," Obama said in the post. "The full weight of the federal government is being brought down on a law-abiding elected official because she has dared to criticize the president."
175 DEMOCRATS DEMAND TRUMP ADMIN STOP ILHAN OMAR INVESTIGATION, WARN IT COULD HURT HER RE-ELECTION BID

Omar has frequently called the allegations that she married her brother a conspiracy theory promulgated by the political right, including in a statement to Fox News Digital regarding the new investigation last week.

"Rep. Omar has repeatedly and unequivocally denied this baseless, disgusting conspiracy theory," an Omar spokesperson said. "This is a desperate political smear designed to distract from Trump’s failed presidency and two years of Republican failure in Congress. And it’s disgraceful that the media continues to give this lie oxygen."
The same spokesperson did not immediately respond to a Thursday morning request for comment.
Fox News Digital's Andrew Mark Miller contributed to this report.

articles.headline: US workers are less engaged at their jobs than ever — and many are blaming AI, particularly remote and hybrid workers
keyFacts: A Gallup report found US worker engagement fell to 29% in the third quarter of 2026, the lowest level since 2011.
The decline was particularly noticeable among remote and hybrid employees working in organizations that have adopted AI tools.
Gallup concluded that AI adoption may be outpacing the communication and managerial support needed to make it effective.
body: - Gallup report finds US workers are feeling less engaged at work than ever
- Remote and hybrid workers are feeling particularly unenthused
- Lack of clarity on AI is also affecting worker happiness

With wide-ranging layoffs, the risk of AI replacement and cost of living increases, it might be no wonder that many employees are feeling less engaged with their jobs, but new research has shown just how much the dissatisfaction has become.
Gallup’s latest quarterly engagement poll for US workers found job engagement fell to its lowest level since 2011 in the third quarter of 2026.

The measure, which tracks workers’ focus, motivation and enthusiasm for their jobs, found engagement fell to 29% in Q3 2026, with remote and hybrid workers particularly disaffected with the state of things.
Lack of engagement

Although the figure sounds dramatically low, it should be pointed out that the engagement figure is never particularly high in Gallup's report - having peaked at 36% in 2020, the figure then fell to 31% by 2024, before its recent drop.
The company noted that the decline was particularly noticeable among remote and hybrid employees, especially those working in organizations which have adopted AI tools.

Gallup noted engagement fell five points among fully remote employees and two points among hybrid employees, compared with approximately one point among on-site employees and those with jobs that cannot be performed remotely.

This was not the first time such trends had been spotted, as Gallup pointed to its earlier research which found hybrid and fully remote employees have experienced larger declines in clarity of expectations than on-site employees in remote-capable jobs.

"These findings raise the possibility that physical distance can contribute to psychological distance between employees and their organizations, particularly as companies navigate the use of AI at work," it said.
Turning to AI, Gallup noted that although research earlier in 2026 had indicated a potential thawing in engagement with employees and AI, this had now declined.

It found workers in "AI-integrated organizations" were now reporting similar levels of engagement than those who weren't - with hybrid and remote workers again saying they were less happy and engaged.
"U.S. employee engagement has fallen to its lowest level in 15 years, with particularly large declines among hybrid and remote employees in organizations that have adopted AI," the report concludes.

"At the same time, fewer employees report clear expectations or feel that someone at work cares about them. The pattern suggests that AI adoption may be outpacing the communication and managerial support needed to make it effective."

He proceeded to play a montage of clips where Trump has been talking about men’s bodies with the president claiming it’s actually helping candidates … which it isn’t.
This week saw Trump campaigning for Ken Paxton in Texas, a candidate he has previously criticised on many occasions.
Meyers wondered if his “complimentary mood” would mean he might change his tune on Paxton, but alas.
“Are you trying to get this guy elected or are you trying to convince him to jump off a building?” Meyers said. “You’re supposed to be his hype-man, not the mom from Carrie.”
He asked Trump to “put all this nonsense aside and be serious” but played another weird clip of him talking about loving meat.
“How is this real fucking life?’” he said.
He added: “Trump doesn’t care about anything voters care about … because he and his rich friends are making bank.”
Meyers said that Paxton is “cartoonishly corrupt” with reports of him at an event in Dubai with fugitives and the woman he is cheating on his wife with.
But while people might ask how he is considered a force in the race, Meyers reminded viewers that Elon Musk has been throwing millions at Paxton’s campaign.
Musk’s wealth has increased by 52% under Trump and the president has not even tried to hide that “huge companies and the mega-rich” have been profiting during his time in the White House.
He called it “glaringly obvious” that rich people have got richer as the average American is struggling.

Instead, rightwing pundits have decided to focus on Obama’s throwaway comment about the Cheesecake Factory. But Meyers reminded viewers that this week Trump told his fans that they would struggle to afford a meal at Mar-a-Lago.
He finished by saying that if you’re part of the rich elite then you’ve been doing very well under Trump but “everyone else is getting screwed”.

articles.headline: It's all relative: Ohio State's Jaylen McClain proving 'the dark side' defensive instincts run deep in family
keyFacts: Ohio State safety Jaylen McClain recorded his first career sack and forced fumble to help secure a 19-15 win against Indiana.
Ohio State starting quarterback Julian Sayin injured his throwing shoulder and is out indefinitely, leaving coach Ryan Day to decide between two quarterbacks.
Ohio State will play USC on Saturday as the Buckeyes navigate the remainder of their regular-season schedule.
body: Jaylen McClain lined up on the edge, and nobody blocked him.

The Ohio State safety wasn't accustomed to the blitz call, but he made the best of it against Indiana. The defending national champions passed up a 45-yard field goal attempt and kept quarterback Josh Hoover on the field on fourth down, trailing 13-7 in the third quarter.
McClain blitzed, struck Hoover's blindside, and rocked him so hard he coughed up the ball. Ohio State recovered, and the Buckeyes won 19-15, snapping the nation's longest winning streak at 22 games.
It was the first sack and forced fumble of McClain's three-year career.

Twenty-four years earlier, his father made a similar play: an interception against Virginia Tech on the first snap of the Hokies' third overtime possession, sealing a 50-42 upset. It was senior Maurice McClain's first interception of his career after returning to the field just two weeks earlier from a broken leg.
"It was a long recovery back," Jaylen said of his father. "... When the play came to him, he just had to make that play."
So did Jaylen.
New generation, same coaches

Fate can be funny. Cyclical, even. Syracuse's defensive backs coach in 2002 was Tim Walton. Matt Patricia was one of Syracuse's graduate assistants working with the scout team. Now Patricia is Ohio State's defensive coordinator, and Walton is Jaylen McClain's secondary coach.
"[Patricia] is the same guy that he was back then," Maurice McClain told CBS Sports. "He was the guy that when he saw a player down, he'd pick him back up. He was hugging guys. That's just him."
Walton "had a lot more fire to him" in 2002, Maurice said. These days, Maurice describes him as "more like a teacher, if anything. He's a life coach."
Carrying the load
The Buckeyes may need more of what Jaylen and his coaches gave them in Bloomington two weeks ago.

Ohio State might be without its starting quarterback for the rest of the season. Julian Sayin injured his throwing shoulder in the fourth quarter at Indiana and is out indefinitely. Coach Ryan Day had not named a starter as of Tuesday for Saturday night's game at USC, with a decision looming between freshman Luke Fahey, who finished the Indiana game, and Tavien St. Clair. Both could play Saturday, Day said.
Whoever plays, they'll try to become the fourth Ohio State quarterback since 2000 to win his first career start in a true road game, and the first since C.J. Stroud in 2021.
Sayin's loss puts more pressure on the Buckeyes' other players, including Heisman Trophy frontrunner Jeremiah Smith, and on a rebuilt defense with eight new starters.

"We all have to step up, coaches, players. And what does that mean?" Day told reporters this week. "Well, we've got to be on our game more and more. I mean, the margin for error certainly has tightened up. There's no question."

The final month of the regular season leaves little room for a slump in the Big Ten title race and the push for the College Football Playoff. No. 2 Ohio State (6-1, 4-0 Big Ten) has won 13 straight regular-season conference games, the longest active streak in FBS, and its only loss came 24-23 in an epic fourth-quarter breakdown at Texas in September. The road isn't easy. The Buckeyes visit USC on Halloween and host Oregon on Nov. 7.

Interestingly enough, Jaylen's recruitment ran through both of the next two opponents. His father said he first wanted to commit to USC, but the Trojans took another player from California. Oregon also went another direction. Ohio State, Maurice said, was the school "he really wanted," and "it opened up to him at the end."
USC (6-2, 3-2) is coming off a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin in which it ran for minus-17 yards, but Day called the Trojans "as talented a team as I've seen on film."
The burden now shifts to a defense Patricia has rebuilt for a second straight season.

His first Ohio State defense allowed 9.3 points and 219.1 yards per game in 2025, the lowest marks in FBS since Alabama in 2011. Then eight starters left, including Caleb Downs, Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles.

The Buckeyes entered their bye week allowing 13.4 points per game, tied for fifth nationally, and a nation-best 5.2 yards per pass attempt. None of their three October opponents scored more than 15 points on offense.

"It puts a little bit more pressure on the defense because we don't want to have that much pressure on the quarterback," McClain said. "But the spirits are very high. I feel like we're headed in the right direction."

Saturday might be the stiffest test yet for McClain and the secondary. Lincoln Riley's USC offense throws for 303.6 yards per game, second in the Big Ten behind only Ohio State, and quarterback Jayden Maiava has thrown a touchdown pass in 13 straight games.

"I would say this offense stresses you in a lot of different areas," Patricia told reporters. "Sometimes we see offenses that maybe stress you in a couple areas. I feel he does an excellent job of stressing the field horizontally and then obviously being able to push the ball downfield vertically. And he does a really good job of understanding when to do that."
His turn to lead

McClain will be counted on to lead. He played alongside Downs, the defense's leader and 2025 Thorpe Award winner, last season. Before Downs left for the NFL, he told McClain to "take that next step," McClain said.

He has. Through seven games, the junior has 32 tackles, two interceptions, four pass breakups, a sack and a forced fumble. More importantly, he has played his best against the toughest opponents. He forced a turnover in all three of Ohio State's games against ranked opponents: interceptions at Texas and Iowa, then the strip-sack at Indiana. This week, he was named a semifinalist for the Thorpe Award, which Downs won a year ago.

"I feel as though he's the same player. It's just that now he's being seen, you know," Maurice said of his son. "I always said that when I watched Caleb Downs at Alabama, I always told people they had the same type of game. But now it's just that people actually had an opportunity to see him play."
Like their father, Jaylen McClain's younger brothers also play defense: KJ is a safety at Tennessee and Cameron is a defensive end at Seton Hall Prep.
Playing defense and making an impact in big moments runs in the family.
"It's cool to score touchdowns," said Jaylen, "but the dark side is better."

articles.headline: Agent identity startup Mintive lands Cowboy Ventures, Coatue, angels Jeff Dean, Andrej Karpathy
keyFacts: Agent identity startup Mintive raised $11 million total, including a $7 million seed round led by Cowboy Ventures.
Mintive was founded by Jiquan Ngiam and Vijay Vasudevan to provide governance, provision, and identity management for enterprise AI agents.
Mintive stated that it has gained 50 enterprise customers since launching its product in February.
body: Here’s another early-stage, agent-management startup to watch because of the backgrounds of the founders and the sheer number of big names it has already attracted as investors: Mintive.

Mintive has raised $11 million total, including a newly announced $7 million seed led by Cowboy Ventures. Additional investors include Coatue, Operator Collective, Hustle Fund, and angels include Okta co-founder Frederic Kerrest, Discovery Loop co-founder and former Google Chief Scientist Jeff Dean, and OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy, among others.

Mintive was founded by Jiquan Ngiam (pictured above, far right) and Vijay Vasudevan (pictured above far left). Ngiam, Mintive’s CEO, was the founding engineer of Coursera (employee No. 1, hired by Andrew Ng). Ngiam later worked on neural networks at Google Brain. Vasudevan, the company’s CTO, is best known as one of the co-creators of TensorFlow while he was at Google Brain. That was the OG AI training platform that predated PyTorch.

Mintive is joining a crowded field of products that promise to govern, provision, and offer identity management to enterprise AI agents. Its platform includes an MCP gateway that allows IT professionals to authorize what the cloud services agents may access and what actions they can perform on them. It also offers an LLM gateway that routes to different models and can cap costs; handles agent identities and authorizations that may differ from the employees that they serve; and an agent monitor that tracks all agents across the company. The company also allows enterprises to create agents that proactively perform long-running tasks.

Still, it’s hard to imagine a field with more competition. Agent management systems are offered by Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, plus as point products galore (from companies as diverse as Langchain, New Relic, Rippling, to name a few). Then there are countless startups working on the idea (40+ from Y Combinator alone).

So, what’s Mintive’s secret sauce? Given the founders’ long history in building AI for enterprises, they have designed their system to be especially easy to use, Ngiam says. Set-up amounts to clicking a few buttons, the startup promises.

“I think what our customers look at and they are a bit shocked at, is how quick it is and easy to deploy,” Ngiam tells TechCrunch. “We have really thought through all the ways this can be done, all the access control, permissioning layer, to make it so easy for them to deploy it, that all the complexities are hidden away. You don’t think about sandboxes, you don’t think about harnesses, you don’t think about memory because we manage that for you.”

That pitch has won over 50 enterprise customers so far, Mintive says, since the startup launched its product in February. These include Ro, Modern Treasury, the University of Michigan, Coursera, Apax, and Stability AI.
But it was the founders’ industry experience that won over Cowboy Ventures managing partner Aileen Lee.
“AI is going to be able to power incredible things, but we need more infrastructure that’s going to give us governance and visibility and control,” Lee told TechCrunch.

Lee also says she particularly respects that Ngiam has been careful by only raising $11 million. This compares to other agentic-building startups raising vast amounts at unicorn valuations. As just one example: Prime Intellect raised $130 million for its Series A at $1 billion valuation.
“I feel really lucky to have won the chance to work with him,” said Lee. “He is a grown-up and so he was not a person chasing a ‘vanity’ round.”

Lee added: “I think a lot of companies are being set up for failure by chasing round size, rather than, ‘how much do I need to actually really move the needle for the company?’ And so, yes, in a time when people are raising unprecedented amounts of money, we’re just kind of doing it the brick by brick, old-fashioned way.”

articles.headline: Built to bend: Postgres’s inventor and a steward on what AI really needs
keyFacts: Michael Stonebraker stated that his team achieved zero-percent accuracy when testing text-to-SQL on MIT's data warehouse using real queries.
Stonebraker and Bruce Momjian argued in upcoming podcast episodes that future AI systems must rely on flexible, community-controlled database architectures.
PostgreSQL 19 prioritized reliability over new features by reverting several previewed capabilities in its latest release.
body: Michael Stonebraker introduced Postgres ® at Berkeley in 1986. Forty years later, the database he invented is a leading choice for a generation of AI projects, and he is among the sharpest skeptics of how those projects are being built. Bruce Momjian is cofounder and core team member of the PostgreSQL Global Development Group, and he works at EnterpriseDB (EDB). In upcoming episodes of AI & Data Horizons by EnterpriseDB (EDB), the Turing Award winner and MIT professor and the Postgres community advocate both make the case that the future belongs to systems that bend without breaking, and to communities that no single company controls.
Zero, not 80

Stonebraker’s first exhibit is text-to-SQL, the promise that a business user can ask a question in plain English and get an answer from the warehouse. Public benchmarks such as Spider and BIRD report accuracy above 80 percent. His team tried the same thing on MIT’s own data warehouse—1,400 tables of student, faculty, building, and salary information—using real queries from its SQL log.

“We got zero-percent accuracy. Not 80, not 70, not 40—zero,” he said. Adding agentic AI, retrieval, and prompt engineering lifted that level into the teens. Telling the model every table and join term reached the 30s. “Still not ready for prime time.”

The reasons are the stuff of every enterprise estate. There is no training data, because the warehouse is not on the public internet. The data is idiosyncratic: among other things, MIT buildings have numbers, not names. The schema has rotted into cryptic table and column names and overlapping views. And real queries are harder than benchmark ones. His team has published its own benchmark, Beaver, and says nobody has broken out of accuracy levels in the 30-percent range.
Use the model for what it’s good at

The deeper problem, Stonebraker argues, is architectural. Large language models are good with text, but “what they are no good at is doing joins of structured data,” which is most of what an enterprise holds. Working with the city of Munich’s transport department, Stonebraker’s team found that answering a single citizen complaint about crosswalk timing meant combining regulations, CAD drawings, trolley schedules, and school-zone maps. Orchestrating that with a language model at the center was, he said, “ridiculously expensive.”

The team’s answer, a system called Rubicon, uses models only on text, then casts the results into tables and hands the rest to a tabular engine. The orchestrator “looks like a query optimizer.” Stonebraker says it is cheaper by a factor of 10 and considerably more accurate than agent frameworks built around a model.

He expects agentic AI to slide from the top of the hype cycle into the valley of despair before a more balanced view emerges. Enterprises hate non-determinism: Approve a loan and reverse it on review, and “that’s called a lawsuit.” Organizations also need protection from rogue agents. The guardrails inside the database, he notes, largely exist already: decades of access control, complete logs, and triggers that can stop a transaction in its tracks. Data-heavy agents, he suggests, belong inside the data layer as user-defined functions, if the tooling to debug and version them improves.

Stonebraker is equally blunt about the frontier. The models have already used the real training data on the internet, and he knows of no enterprise that will let a model train on its proprietary data. AGI, he said, is “basically marketing hype” from foundation model vendors justifying their valuations.
Nobody owns it

Why Postgres ? “Postgres is the intergalactic answer to open source,” Stonebraker said. Its unique feature is that “it’s not controlled by any one company.” EDB, Microsoft, Google, and others each contribute committers, and nobody steers. He dates its rise to Oracle buying MySQL, when “everybody said: vendor control.” For enterprises, that independence is the foundation of sovereignty : retaining control over how and where their data systems operate.

Momjian describes the same structure from the inside. Postgres has no office, no assets, and no legal entity, yet it produces “software better than billion-dollar companies.” Its forecasting tool is the community itself, which spots needs early from China, Russia, and the United States. “We only need one person in the world to be supersmart, and that person to tell us what they think.”
Built to bend

Both experts describe a design philosophy that favors flexibility over the last few percent of speed. Stonebraker built Postgres to be extended, and that is why it absorbed JSON, full-text search, GIS, and now AI without a rewrite. Momjian adds a second call from the 1990s: Lean on the operating system rather than absorb it, which made Postgres a natural fit for the cloud.

Momjian resists optimizations that buy 5 or 10 percent at the cost of rigidity, since a mistuned system can lose 40 percent. “If you take a Formula One car to the supermarket, there’s no place for the groceries.” The project plans on a horizon few vendors can match. “We’re looking at what would be the impact 5 years from now, 10 years from now.”
What PostgreSQL 19 delivers

The new release puts that discipline on show. Several previewed features, including SQL property graph queries and partition merging and splitting, were reverted, because reliability comes first. AI-assisted review is finding problems quickly; the August 2026 patch release for PostgreSQL 18 addressed 28 CVEs.

What remains is practical: REPACK CONCURRENTLY for busy tables, smarter parallel autovacuum, and sequence synchronization for logical replication. Plan Advice, from PostgreSQL major contributor and committer Robert Haas, is the community’s answer to Oracle-style optimizer hints it rejected for years. “Somebody found a way of doing it that didn’t have the downsides,” Momjian said.
The database as AI’s memory

The two diverge on how fast AI will write SQL. Momjian expects agents to create databases and generate much of the code. Stonebraker says that will not happen inside the enterprise until data is documented, silos are opened, and the politics change. They agree on the destination. AI needs a relational system to give it permanence and memory, and, in Momjian’s words, that is “a game-changer.”
Forty years on, the inventor and the steward are betting on the same database.
Contributed by EnterpriseDB

articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed’s father is board member of charity accused of funneling cash to Saddam Hussein
keyFacts: Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed’s father serves on the board of Life for Relief and Development, a charity previously accused of funneling cash to Saddam Hussein's regime.
The charity reached a $780,000 settlement with the US government in 2014 after facing investigations, raids, and accusations regarding sanctions and money-laundering violations.
The New York Post reported that the campaign of Abdul El-Sayed and the charity were contacted for comment.
body: WASHINGTON — Michigan Senate hopeful Abdul El-Sayed’s father sits on the board of an Islamic charity that was previously accused of funneling cash to late Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein’s regime.
Imam Dr. Mohammed El-Sayed is currently a board member of Life for Relief and Development, a charity he’s worked with since at least 2020, according to tax forms.

In 2004, the US military and FBI raided Life for Relief and Development’s Baghdad facilities, confiscating 20 boxes and 12 computers amid suspicions that the charity had been aiding insurgents, the San Francisco Chronicle reported.

Later, the Islamic charity’s public relations coordinator Muthanna al-Hanooti faced charges for serving as an unregistered agent for Hussein’s government and pleaded guilty to flouting the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.
Life for Relief and Development was accused by the US government of concocting a conspiracy to funnel funds from America through Jordan and into Hussein’s Iraq.

“LRD’s highest management levels—i.e., its President—knew of the conduct giving rise to the apparent violations and directed the funds transfers to Iraq via Jordan,” the government noted around the time.
The group eventually reached a $780,000 settlement with the US government, which dropped its case against the charity in 2014.
The senior El-Sayed’s ties to the Islamic charity that sent money into Hussein’s Iraq were first reported by the Washington Free Beacon.
In addition to its history of sending money to Hussein’s regime, Life for Relief and Development has been accused of other ties to terrorism.
In 2006, the Michigan-based charity was raided by the FBI and, in 2007, its then-CEO was indicted by a grand jury for flouting money-laundering and sanctions laws.

The feds confiscated “correspondence, notes, e-mails, facsimiles and other documents and records” pertaining to the Islamic African Relief Agency, a group that was later shuttered after being exposed for supporting al Qaeda.
El-Sayed’s birth mother, Fatten Fathy Elkomy, briefly worked at the Islamic African Relief Agency.
The Life for Relief and Development also sent cash to an entity that the FBI later concluded was Hamas’ Jordanian operation, as The Post previously reported.
El-Sayed’s father-in-law, Jukaku Tayeb, also once served on the Life for Relief and Development’s board.
The Post has contacted El-Sayed’s campaign and the Life for Relief and Development for comment.
El-Sayed currently has a 3.2 percentage point polling edge over Republican foe Mike Rogers, according to the latest RealClearPolitics polling aggregate.

articles.headline: Greetings from Baghdad, where Agatha Christie's old home presents its own mystery
keyFacts: Iraq's culture ministry stated that an abandoned house on the Tigris River in Baghdad is the former home of English novelist Agatha Christie.
The heritage property is currently padlocked, falling down, and has been left to decay over the last century.
The Iraqi government stated that it is willing to make the house available to anyone who will restore it.
body: Greetings from Baghdad, where Agatha Christie's old home presents its own mystery
This, according to Iraq's culture ministry, is the one-time home of English mystery novelist Agatha Christie, on the banks of the Tigris River in Baghdad.
Fittingly, the abandoned house has its own mystery: why it's been left to decay over the last century.

Christie made dozens of trips to Iraq, including the one where she met her archaeologist husband, Max Mallowan, in 1930. They Came to Baghdad and Murder in Mesopotamia were two of her novels set in Iraq.

As for the house, it's a heritage property controlled by Iraq's culture ministry. The Iraqi government says it's willing to make the house available to anyone who will restore it. It is padlocked and literally falling down.
When we visited this month, there was a $200 electricity bill stuffed into a hole in the door — apparently reflecting years of unpaid bills in its more recent history.

articles.headline: Maine, Kansas Senate races neck and neck as Democrats lead in Texas, Michigan, poll shows
keyFacts: Senate races in Maine and Kansas are extremely close, while Democrats hold leads in Texas and Michigan, according to a CNN poll.
Democrats need to flip four Senate seats from red to blue to gain a 51-seat majority in the chamber.
CNN conducted its telephone polling between October 20 and October 27 with hundreds of likely voters across the four states.
body: High-profile races that will determine which party controls the Senate for the next two years are extremely tight, according to a new CNN poll , as Maine and Kansas remain close and Democrats extended their leads in Texas and Michigan.

Democrats, who are widely projected to win a majority in the House of Representatives, need to flip four Senate seats from red to blue in order to gain a 51-seat majority, protecting their majority from the vice presidential tiebreaker.
In Maine, Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, is the only Republican incumbent running in a state that went for Kamala Harris in 2024.
FOX NEWS POLL: NAIL-BITER IN MAINE SENATE RACE
Collins' Democratic challenger is Troy Jackson, the former president of the state Senate who jumped into the race as a replacement for the previous nominee, scandal-plagued Graham Platner .
The race has no clear frontrunner, according to the CNN poll, though Jackson holds a marginal lead.
COLLINS INSISTS SOCIALIST RIVAL WON'T BEAT HER AS MAINE'S MONEY MACHINE: 'YOU'LL LOSE BIG TIME'

Forty-nine percent of respondents told the outlet's pollsters they favored Jackson, compared to 45% for Collins. While Jackson is slightly ahead, at least 12.5% of voters say they could still change their minds.

Respondents tied Collins to her party less than any other Republican running for Senate in the nation, with 46% of respondents saying they believe she would choose her constituents over the Republican Party.
DAVID MARCUS: THE FUTURE OF THE GOP IN NEW ENGLAND RIDES ON MAINE’S SENATE VOTE

Collins was one of seven Republicans to vote in favor of President Donald Trump's second impeachment in 2021, and she joined Sen. Lisa Murkowski, R-Alaska, as the only Republicans to vote against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth's Senate confirmation in 2025.

With Collins managing to distance herself from Trump, her race has largely become a referendum on her own career. Three-quarters of respondents from either party told CNN pollsters that their choice was motivated more by Collins than Jackson.
DAVID MARCUS: IN BLUE MAINE, NOBODY BELIEVES SUSAN COLLINS WILL LOSE UNTIL THEY SEE IT
In Michigan, despite warnings from some mainstream Democrats and the state's Jewish community, Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed is building a lead over former Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich.

Respondents favored El-Sayed at 49% compared to the 42% who favored Rogers, according to the poll. CNN's previous poll, released in early September, showed El-Sayed with a 47% share compared to Rogers' 44%, showing the former public health director El-Sayed building on his lead.
FOX NEWS POLL: MICHIGAN VOTERS SPLIT BETWEEN EL-SAYED AND ROGERS

The Democrat has consolidated his party's support after a contentious primary with Rep. Haley Stevens , D-Mich. Ninty-five percent of likely Democrat voters say they'll punch the ticket for El-Sayed, up from 90% in the September poll.

Rogers voters, meanwhile, are motivated more by dislike for the Democratic candidate than faith in the Republican. 57% told CNN pollsters they were voting against El-Sayed, up from 41% in a previous poll.
DAVID MARCUS: THE 5 FACTORS THAT COULD DECIDE MICHIGAN'S TIGHT AND UGLY SENATE RACE
Rogers' favorability has also taken a hit, moving from 58% in September to 50% in October.
Texas State Rep. James Talarico also built upon a narrow lead over Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton, despite Talarico's extended absence from the campaign trail in early October.
FOX NEWS POLL: TEXAS SENATE RACE GALLOPING TOWARD A PHOTO FINISH
Forty-nine percent of likely voters told pollsters they'd vote for Talarico, while 43% said they would vote for Paxton, according to the poll.

Texas, a state that has voted for exactly one new Democratic Senate candidate into office since Lyndon B. Johnson vacated his seat to become vice president, also voted more strongly for Trump in 2024 than in either of his previous elections.
TRUMP WON THIS RELIABLY RED STATE BY DOUBLE DIGITS. NOW A DEADLOCKED RACE IS BRINGING HIM BACK
Despite the typically steadfast support for the GOP in the Lone Star State, Talarico is riding a wave of favorability and minority support to remain in pole position five days before polls close.
CNN's poll says 64% of likely voters of color support Talarico, including 22% of the cohort that voted for Trump in 2024.

Talarico is also leading Paxton in favorability within their own parties. 24% of Republicans have an unfavorable view of Paxton, according to the poll. Just 2% of Democrats, meanwhile, view Talarico unfavorably.
In Kansas, a state which Trump won by 16 percentage points in 2024, incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., is falling behind Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton.
Forty-nine percent of likely voters say they support Hamilton, 45% say they support Marshall.

Hamilton, a relatively unknown candidate, is far outperforming his own party in a state where Democrats are broadly unfavorable. 57% of voters view the Democratic Party as unfavorable while only 38% of them feel the same about Hamilton.

Like Republicans in Michigan, likely voters in Kansas appear to be more highly motivated by a dislike for one candidate than strong positive feelings for another. 59% of Hamilton backers say they're motivated by opposition to Marshall.
Hamilton, a Christian pastor , is even drawing support from across the aisle. Roughly 12% of Republicans and Republican-leaning likely voters say they support Hamilton, according to the poll.

CNN conducted its polling via telephone between Oct. 20 and Oct. 27. Registered voters were randomly sampled, according to the outlet. 838 likely voters were considered in Kansas, 783 in Maine, 768 in Michigan and 923 in Texas. CNN tabulated its margins of sampling error at plus or minus 4.5% for Kansas and Maine, 4.7% in Michigan and 4.2% in Texas.
Fox News Digital contacted all eight campaigns for further comment.

articles.headline: The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
keyFacts: The New York Times is testing an AI feature for its Cooking app that suggests ingredient and equipment substitutions and scales serving sizes.
Some users expressed concern over the environmental and user experience impacts of AI, and whether the feature could be disabled.
NYT spokesperson Jordan Cohen stated that the optional feature is currently available to iOS subscribers while the company monitors performance.
body: The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it’s sparked some drama among users. NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature last Friday, which can be used to recommend substitutions for ingredients and cooking equipment, scale recipes to any number of servings, and “generally make our recipes work for what a cook needs at that moment.”
The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
Some users aren’t exactly thrilled with the New York Times’ recipe tweaking AI tool.

One of the examples given in the article shows a user asking to use baby spinach instead of kale, with the NYT Cooking app feature advising that because baby spinach wilts faster, it should be added during a later step of the recipe. Ko says it can also change the recipes around different pans and tools. Customized recipes are private and can’t be published or shared via the app. The AI modification feature is being rolled out gradually while the NYT monitors how it performs — it’s currently available to all Cooking subscribers on the iOS app, and will be more broadly available “soon.”

Some NYT readers have pushed back against the feature, citing concerns in the article’s comment section around the environmental impact of widespread AI adoption and the general impact that AI features may have on the user experience. When one user asked if there will be a way to disable the AI feature, Ko responded with “No, not at this time,” and noted that the feature is “completely optional to use.”

“Unbelievably disappointing to see,” said another NYT user. “I’ve always loved NYT Cooking and it pains me that the AI mandate has reached what used to be a wonderful and simple collection of recipes and notes from all sorts of different people.”

This isn’t the first time that AI has been used by the NYT Cooking app. Ko says it was used to convert imperial volume measurements to metric weight measurements in recipes two years ago, and a feature was added last year that converts recipes to halve or double the original serving size. The comments on the new AI feature announcement post have since been closed, but NYT spokesperson Jordan Cohen tells The Verge that this is standard practice:

“Comments on this article remained open for four days, with editors from Cooking taking care to answer questions, address concerns and engage directly with readers. We kept that conversation open to give readers a meaningful opportunity to share feedback and hear from the team. Closing comments on older articles is standard practice at The Times so that our moderators can focus on new discussions. We’re pleased to see that many members of our Cooking community are interested in exploring this tool and are already trying it out on our iOS app; they’re reporting good results.”

articles.headline: 'Fully committed' Fernandes to remain Man Utd captain
keyFacts: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick stated that Bruno Fernandes remains fully committed to the club and will continue serving as captain.
Carrick held talks with Fernandes following a team defeat and maintained that the captaincy is not in question, though his starting place remains uncertain.
Carrick will remain in charge for upcoming matches after discussions with club leadership following an eight-game winless run.
body: - Published
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick says Bruno Fernandes is "fully committed" to the club and will continue as captain.
Carrick dropped Fernandes to the bench for Sunday's 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth after the Portuguese questioned the tactics used in a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como.
The defeat by Bournemouth left Carrick's future hanging by a thread, but the 45-year-old will be in charge for Saturday's trip to Chelsea.
It remains to be seen whether Fernandes will return to the starting line-up, but the pair held clear-the-air talks at United's Carrington training ground on Tuesday in a bid to move forward.
Carrick says there is "no decision to be made" over whether Fernandes remains captain.
"We are clear with the situation of the team, and as a football club," said Carrick.
"He [Fernandes] is an important player for this group. He has been and he will be.
"We've got to make a difference and we've got to push things in a good direction.
"He's fully committed to this football club; he's fully committed to making things better. There are absolutely no issues with that.
"It doesn't change for me. It was a decision for what we felt for the [Bournemouth] game. That's it.
"He's the one that's led the team so well for many a game and many a year, and he'll continue to do that. There are absolutely no issues with that."
Carrick 'doesn't need assurances' over future
United have gone eight games without a win as they head to Chelsea - their worst run of results since 2015-16.
Not since the 1988-89 campaign have they had a sequence of nine matches without a win.

Nearly 40 hours passed between United losing against Bournemouth on Sunday and the club providing clarification on Carrick's future, with the Englishman being given a chance to turn things around at Old Trafford.
Talks involving the Glazer family, minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox took place before Carrick's immediate future was confirmed.

It seems likely he will remain in post for next Tuesday's Champions League match against Roma, and the Premier League encounter with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on 8 November, after which there is a two-week international break.
Carrick, though, says he does not need guarantees over his position.
"I don't need any assurances from anyone," he said.
"I totally get the position. I understand the job. I understand the responsibilities. I understand what comes with that. So, I really don't need any assurances from anyone in that regard."

Asked if he was surprised to still be in a job, Carrick said: "No. I'm here to do my job. I'm here to do the best for the team, and I'm desperate to make us better and improve things. So, I'm not surprised, no."

articles.headline: Germany seeks new head of state
keyFacts: Germany's federal government is seeking a successor for current President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, whose term ends in early 2027.
Chancellor Friedrich Merz's center-right CDU holds the right to nominate a candidate for the largely ceremonial head of state position.
Government sources said discussions will be held with state chairpersons and other parties ahead of meetings scheduled for November 9.
body: Wanted: A new head of state — female, male, or other. Requirements: German citizen, entitled to vote, minimum age 40. Please apply as soon as possible! Availability starting January 30, 2027; job starts March 19, 2027.

This is not an official job posting, but Germany's federal government is indeed looking for someone to fill the nation's highest office. Having already served two terms, current President Frank-Walter Steinmeier is no longer eligible for another, leaving the position open for a successor. Many feel that it is time for Germany's first-ever female head of state.

"The person should have a certain level of public recognition, be politically unbiased, capable of bringing people together, approachable and a reasonably good [public] speaker," political scientist Ursula Münch told DW.

In Germany, a federal parliamentary republic, the president serves as head of state and a representative of the country as well as someone who embodies moral authority for the nation. Unlike for instance in the US, France, or Russia, the president does not wield extensive political power or direct government affairs.

Steinmeier was nominated by his own party, the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD), in 2009. However, once elected via a convention of parliamentarians and state electors, a president-elect has to suspend their party membership in order to serve in the office apolitically. This time, it is Chancellor Friedrich Merz's center-right Christian Democrats (CDU), the power broker in the coalition government with the SPD and the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU), which has the right to nominate a candidate.

Political scientist Münch says that "the three parties must agree on a person who is acceptable for all three." Since the convention that will select Steinmeier's successor is currently controlled by these three parties and their delegates, it is very likely that whoever Merz nominates will be elected.
Will Germany soon have its first female president?

"Well, I would really like it to be a woman this time. We've had 12 male federal presidents since 1949 — it's about time for a woman! But if the right man were to be nominated, I'd be fine with that too," says Münch. According to an August poll conducted by the Forsa polling institute for the RTL television network, about 74% of German respondents say they don't care whether it's a man or a woman. Another 19% explicitly want a woman, while 5% prefer a man.

Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner appears to have a good chance. She is president of the Bavarian State Parliament in Munich. Aigner is a member of the smallest party in the coalition, the Bavarian CSU, and is considered a unifying figure. She also has experience in government in Berlin, having served as agricultural minister at the federal level. She enjoys strong support within her Bavarian CSU party, whose leader Markus Söder recently said: "It would be tremendous if she became federal president."

Even members of the opposition Greens and the SPD are full of praise for Aigner's candidacy. "What are we actually waiting for? Surely Ilse Aigner has long since secured a majority across party lines?" asked SPD parliamentary group leader Matthias Miersch recently. However, Merz, who is friends with Aigner, has remained tight-lipped so far — possibly also because Aigner is not a member of Merz's party, but rather of its smaller sister party, the CSU.
Several female presidential candidates

Other potential successors from the CDU membership have also been mentioned: Bundestag President Julia Klöckner, former Defense Minister Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer and Education Minister Karin Prien. Hesse's state premier, Boris Rhein, is also a possible candidate. In recent days, another name has been making the rounds: lawyer Ines Claus, who serves as CDU's parliamentary group leader in Hesse and deputy party chair at the federal level — and is largely unknown.

However, rumors that she would be nominated were swiftly shot down by the chancellor. Sources close to Merz emphasized that he has so far "neither made a decision nor put forward a proposal." There are "a number of suitable" options, sources added.

The president is elected every five years by the Federal Convention, which comprises all 630 members of the Bundestag and an equal number of electors who represent the state parliaments. Among them are also prominent figures from the spheres of culture, science, sports and society. The candidate who receives more than 631 votes goes on to assume office. The governing parties — the CDU/CSU and the SPD — have a combined total of 682 votes, a comfortable majority.
Presidential role key amid polarization and crisis

The office of the president is often underestimated as merely a ceremonial role. Yet, as an authority standing above the political parties, this person wields considerable political, legal and moral influence. This is especially true in times of political polarization and international crises. While the president does not govern like a chancellor, he or she represents Germany both at home and abroad.

"From a constitutional perspective, the federal president is enormously important. For example, in a political crisis, he could decide whether it makes more sense to dissolve the Bundestag or to advocate for a minority government," explains political scientist Münch. In addition, he reviews and signs laws proposed by politicians.
What happens next?

The federal chancellor and CDU chairman has an interest in an orderly process, say sources close to the government. The "first milestone" will be the meetings of the CDU Presidium and Executive Board on November 9. Until then, discussions will be held with the state chairpersons of the CDU and the CSU. Sources made it clear that the SPD and the Greens will also be consulted, "since the election of the federal president should have broad support across the democratic spectrum."
That is how political scientist Münch sees it: "I still consider the question open, with a slight edge for CSU candidate Ilse Aigner." But there could still be a real surprise, Münch adds.
This article was originally published in German.

articles.headline: Garcia 'open minded' about PGA Tour return and reveals Ryder Cup target
keyFacts: Sergio Garcia announced he is leaving LIV Golf and will play on the DP World Tour for the 2027 season.
Garcia stated he is open-minded about a potential return to the PGA Tour following a 12-month suspension.
Garcia expressed his ambition to secure a spot on Luke Donald's European Ryder Cup team for the 2027 tournament.
body: LIV Golf: Sergio Garcia 'open minded' about PGA Tour return as he targets 2027 Ryder Cup after breakaway league exit

Sergio Garcia has announced his intention to play on the DP World Tour in 2027 following his LIV Golf departure; the 46-year-old Spaniard is looking to secure a spot on Luke Donald's European Ryder Cup team for next year's tournament at Adare Manor
Thursday 29 October 2026 15:34, UK
Sergio Garcia is returning to the DP World Tour for the 2027 season and is open-minded about getting a place back on the PGA Tour, too.

The 46-year-old Spaniard revealed his future plans in a statement on his social media accounts on Thursday. His departure from LIV Golf was already known after four years playing on the breakaway circuit.
"Next season, I'll be playing on the DP World Tour," Garcia wrote. "This tour has been a huge part of my career from the very beginning, and I'm proud to call it home again.
"I'm also keeping my options open for a return to the PGA Tour. And probably the most exciting part for me is strengthening my personal relationships, both new and old."

Garcia, who said he was "putting a big focus on a strong mindset and my mental health," also expressed his ambition to secure a spot on Luke Donald's European Ryder Cup team for the 2027 tournament at Adare Manor.
The Spaniard is Team Europe's all-time leading Ryder Cup points scorer with 28.5 points across 10 appearances, with his last coming at Whistling Straits in 2021.

Garcia's statement made reference to an incident at this year's Masters, where he broke his driver on the second hole at Augusta National after an outburst on the tee box. He was later issued with a code-of-conduct warning - a first at the tournament.

"I can't wait to get back to The Masters," added Garcia, who won the Green Jacket in 2017. "I left Augusta (in 2026) disappointed with myself and my actions, and I'm ready to show what I've learned and where I am mentally.
"Augusta has given me some of the greatest moments of my life, and I'd love nothing more than to chase another green jacket at such a special place."
The Spaniard was one of the most high-profile players to join LIV Golf in 2022.

His last start on the PGA Tour, outside of the majors, came at the Wells Fargo Championship that year. During that tournament, Garcia struck an errant approach shot into a patch of long grass and was overheard venting, "I can't wait to leave this tour," while looking for his ball.
Garcia, who has 11 career PGA Tour wins, will be forced to wait until August 2027 before he can make his return, due to the US circuit's 12-month suspension on LIV Golfers.
The circuit is emerging from Chapter 11 bankruptcy with BC Partners Credit and its $300 million pledge, and without Saudi money. Garcia had already sought - and been granted - approval to leave LIV.
Jon Rahm, Louis Oosthuizen, Ian Poulter and Tyrrell Hatton are among other high-profile players to announce their exits from LIV.
